title: What Is CTV Advertising? | Your Complete Connected TV Dictionary

facts.fact: CTV ads are non-skippable video advertisements served within streaming TV content, typically running 15 or 30 seconds and appearing full-screen, according to Paramount Ads Manager's glossary.
facts.quote: CTV ads are non-skippable video advertisements served within streaming TV content. They typically run for 15 or 30 seconds and appear full-screen.

facts.fact: Paramount's glossary recommends a strong opening hook within the first 3–5 seconds of a CTV ad to engage streaming viewers.
facts.quote: Strong opening hook in the first 3–5 seconds

facts.fact: Paramount's glossary gives frequency capping as an example of no more than 3 impressions per household per day.
facts.quote: (For example: No more than 3 impressions per household per day).

facts.fact: Paramount's glossary defines CTV CPM (cost per thousand impressions) as (Total Spend ÷ Impressions) × 1,000.
Paramount's glossary defines ROAS as Revenue ÷ Ad Spend.
facts.quote: ROAS calculation formula: Revenue ÷ Ad Spend

facts.fact: Paramount's glossary defines video completion rate (VCR) as Completed Views ÷ Total Impressions.
Paramount's glossary states that geo-targeting can include Country, State, DMA (Designated Market Area), ZIP code, or radius targeting around a specific address.
facts.quote: including Country, State, DMA (Designated Market Area), ZIP code, or radius targeting around a specific address.

facts.fact: Paramount's glossary states that CTV ad targeting can be based on household-level filters such as ZIP code, age, gender, and income.
facts.quote: Household-level targeting (ZIP code, age, gender, income)

facts.fact: Paramount's glossary describes a device graph as connecting multiple devices, such as a connected TV, mobile phone, laptop, or tablet, to a single household or user profile.
facts.quote: connect multiple devices (whether that's a connected TV, mobile phone, laptop, or tablet) to a single household or user profile.

facts.fact: Media buying is the process of purchasing advertising inventory across channels such as connected TV, social media, search, or display.
facts.quote: Media buying is the process of purchasing advertising inventory across channels such as connected TV, social media, search, or display.

facts.fact: All CTV is OTT, but not all OTT is CTV, according to the page's definition of the two terms.
facts.quote: All CTV is OTT, but not all OTT is CTV.

facts.fact: Subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) services are subscription-based with limited or no advertising.
facts.quote: Subscription-based services with limited or no advertising.

facts.fact: Ad-supported video-on-demand (AVOD) services are free or lower-cost streaming services supported by ads.
facts.quote: Free or lower-cost streaming services supported by ads.

facts.fact: Free ad-supported streaming TV (FAST) channels are free for viewers and supported entirely by advertising, with Pluto TV given as an example.
facts.quote: Streaming channels that are free for viewers and supported entirely by advertising (i.e. Pluto TV).

facts.fact: Programmatic advertising uses automated technology to buy and serve ads in real time, with the platform purchasing inventory that matches advertiser-set criteria.
facts.quote: Programmatic advertising uses automated technology to buy and serve ads in real time.

facts.fact: Sequential messaging is a strategy where viewers see a planned series of ads in a specific order.
facts.quote: Sequential messaging is a strategy where viewers see a planned series of ads in a specific order.

facts.fact: According to the page, a self-serve advertising platform does not mean unsupported, since many platforms offer help centers, onboarding tools, or optional support teams.
